# United Kingdom Property Market Profile

## Structural Characteristics
- Population: ~68M | Housing stock: ~25M dwellings
- Homeownership rate: ~65% (down from 71% peak in 2003)
- Owner-occupation declining, private rental sector growing (PRS ~19% now)
- Dominant mortgage: 2-5 year fixed rate (~90%+ of new lending), then reverts to SVR
- Key institutions: ONS (HPI), HM Land Registry, Bank of England (FPC macroprudential), Nationwide/Halifax (lender indices)

## Historical Cycle Phases

| Period | Phase | Key Driver |
|--------|-------|------------|
| 1996-2007 | Mega-boom (+180% real) | Financial deregulation, buy-to-let, credit boom |
| 2008-2009 | Correction (-18%) | GFC, credit crunch |
| 2010-2016 | Recovery (+40%) | Low rates, Help to Buy, foreign money (London) |
| 2017-2019 | Flat/Correction (London -15%) | Brexit uncertainty, stamp duty changes, affordability ceiling |
| 2020-2022 | Boom (+25%) | Stamp duty holiday, "race for space," low rates |
| 2022-2024 | Correction (-3-5% nominal, -10-15% real) | BOE aggressive hiking (0.1% → 5.25%), mortgage rate shock |
| 2024-2025 | Stabilization | Rates declining, supply still tight |

## Key UK-Specific Drivers

### 1. Mortgage Market Structure
- 2-5 year fixed rates dominant (~90%+), then revert to SVR (typically 7-8% currently)
- ~1.5M households face fixed-rate expiry each year
- Mortgage rate shock: fixed-rate expiry from 1.5% to 5-6% → £200-400/month increase
- Unlike US: no 30-year fix → regular refinancing required
- Unlike AU/NZ: short fixes provide rate certainty for 2-5 years, but cliff at expiry

### 2. Chronic Housing Undersupply
- 300,000 new homes/year target (all governments since 2010s — never met)
- Actual delivery: ~200-240K/year in England
- Planning system (Town & Country Planning Act 1947 and successors) = major constraint
- Green belt restrictions around major cities
- SME builder sector decimated since GFC (down from ~12,000 to ~2,500)
- Nutrient neutrality rules (2019-) blocked 50-100K+ homes

### 3. London vs Rest of UK Divergence
| Metric | London | Rest of UK |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| Median Price | £520K | £250-300K |
| Price-to-Income | ~12-14x | ~6-8x |
| Price Change since 2017 | -5% to flat | +15-25% |
| Foreign Buyer Share | 10-15% (prime central) | < 2% |
| Rental Yields | 3-4% | 4-6% |

London had its correction first (2016-2020: Brexit, stamp duty surcharge, COVID exodus). The rest of the UK boomed during COVID (race for space) and is now correcting as rates bite.

### 4. Build-to-Rent (BTR) — Growing Institutional Sector
- Fastest-growing housing tenure in the UK
- Institutional landlords building entire apartment blocks for rental
- ~100K BTR units completed, ~150K in pipeline
- Concentrated in London, Manchester, Birmingham
- US model adapted for UK (Greystar, Related, Legal & General)

### 5. Leasehold Reform
- England: Leasehold system for flats (unique vs Scotland's outright ownership)
- Ground rent scandal: doubling ground rents trapped leaseholders
- Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024: ground rents capped, lease extensions easier
- Ban on new leasehold houses (not flats) from 2024

## Key Data Sources

| Data | Source | Frequency | Notes |
|------|--------|----------|-------|
| UK HPI | ONS / HM Land Registry | Monthly | Official, most comprehensive but lagged |
| Nationwide HPI | Nationwide BS | Monthly | Faster, mortgage-approval based |
| Halifax HPI | Halifax | Monthly | Similar to Nationwide |
| RICS Residential Survey | RICS | Monthly | Forward-looking survey (price expectations, enquiries, sales) |
| BOE Mortgage Approvals | BOE | Monthly | Leading indicator — approvals → transactions with 2-3 month lag |
| Rental Index | ONS / Zoopla | Monthly | ONS official, Zoopla faster |
| Housing Supply Indicators | DLUHC | Quarterly | Starts, completions, planning permissions |

## Affordability Benchmarks

| Metric | London | South East | Midlands/North | National |
|--------|--------|-----------|---------------|----------|
| Median Price | £500-550K | £350-400K | £200-250K | £280-300K |
| Price-to-Income | ~12-14x | ~8-10x | ~5-7x | ~7-8x |
| Price-to-Rent | ~25-30x | ~18-22x | ~12-15x | ~18-22x |
| Mortgage % of Income* | 45-55% | 35-45% | 25-30% | 35-40% |

*At 5.5% rate, 25Y, 20% deposit

## BOE Macroprudential Framework (FPC)

| Tool | Current Setting | Impact |
|------|----------------|--------|
| LTI Flow Limit | Max 15% of new mortgages > 4.5× income | Constrains high-multiple lending |
| Affordability Stress Test | Withdrawn (Aug 2022) | Was: 3% above reversion rate |
| Counter-Cyclical Capital Buffer | 2% (neutral rate) | Bank resilience |
| Mortgage Market Review (2014) | Strict affordability verification | Reduced liar loans |

## Key Risks

### Downside
- Mortgage rate cliff: 1.5M+ fixed-rate roll-offs per year at significantly higher rates
- London prime central: political risk (non-dom tax changes, Labour government)
- BTL sector contraction: tax changes (Section 24) + higher rates → landlord exodus
- Cladding/fire safety crisis: 2M+ leaseholders in buildings with defects, remediation slow
- Scottish market: Additional Dwelling Supplement (6%) + rent controls discouraging investment

### Upside
- BOE rate cuts (expected 2025-) → direct mortgage relief
- Chronic undersupply = structural floor under prices in desirable areas
- Stamp duty reform potential (Labour considering replacing with annual property tax)
- Planning reform (Labour's "grey belt" release, mandatory housing targets)
- Leasehold reform removing distortions

### Cycle Assessment
- Phase: Correction → Stabilization
- Correction primarily real (inflation eroding values), not nominal
- London corrected first and earliest, may lead recovery
- Key differentiator: BTL sector contraction is structural, not cyclical — less rental supply, higher rents
- Housing is a generational political issue in the UK — policy intervention likely to increase
